title: PS-18 Impact of implant strategy and backgrounding rate of gain on yearling performance, feedlot performance, and carcass characteristics
content:
Abstract
In a 3-yr study, 179 yearling steers and spayed heifers (n = 146 steers and 33 heifers) were utilized to determine the impact of implant strategy and rate of gain during a wintering backgrounding phase on yearling growth performance, feedlot performance, and carcass characteristics. In January, yearlings were stratified by body weight (BW), blocked by sex, and randomly assigned to one of four treatments. Treatments design was a 2 × 2 factorial arrangement, which included rate of average daily gain (ADG) of 0.455 kg/day (LOW) or 0.910 kg/day (HIGH) and receiving a growth implant (IMP; Compudose (Elanco Animal Health)) or no implant (NOIMP) during the overwinter backgrounding period. After the winter backgrounding period, yearlings were combined for a summer grazing period and then shipped to the feedlot. At the start of the summer grazing period, all yearlings received a growth implant (Component E-S for steers and Component E-H for heifers; Elanco Animal Health). Once in the feedlot, a terminal implant (Component TE-200; Elanco Animal Health) was used approximately 100 d prior to slaughter. Initial BW in January were not different (P ≥ 0.71) by treatments. In May, HIGH yearlings had greater (P < 0.001) BW compared to LOW yearlings and IMP yearlings had greater (P = 0.03) BW compared to NOIMP, which was the result from increased (P ≤ 0.02) over-winter ADG in HIGH and IMP yearlings. In September, HIGH yearlings had greater (P = 0.03) BW, whereas overwinter implant strategy did not influence (P = 0.11) yearling BW. Low-gain yearlings had increased (P < 0.01) summer ADG compared to HIGH yearling with no differences (P = 0.42) between implant strategy. After the finishing period, HIGH yearlings were larger (P = 0.04) than LOW yearlings with no difference by implant strategy (P = 0.35). Treatments did not influence (P ≥ 0.55) feedlot ADG. After the finishing period, High yearlings had larger HCW (P = 0.04) than LOW yearlings with no difference (P = 0.70) by implant strategy. Yield grade exhibited a rate of gain and implant strategy interaction (P = 0.05) with Low/IMP yearlings having the lowest yield grade. Treatments did not influence (P ≥ 0.25) quality grade, marbling, or longissimus muscle area. These results indicate that increased overwinter gains (~0.9 kg/d) increases BW throughout the yearling to finishing phase. Implant strategy impacted growth rate up to summer grazing, however, the increased advantage disappeared throughout the finishing phase.
